After the violence : Xenophobia

By: Jane Lipman | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As Sowetans ,Somalis and Pakistanis pick up the pieces ,Carte Blanche goes behind the headlines into the communities

Summary:
In the week following some of the worst violence against Somalis ,Ethiopians ,Pakistanis in Soweto and Kagiso ,Carte Blanche visits the beareaved families ,the mother who's baby died in the stampede in Soweto ,and a Pakistani family who lost everything and asks what government is doing to help these people in their grief and loss

Further information:
We have accessed Nhlanhla Monarengs family in Naledi ,his mother and father will talk to us and let us film their memorial for 19 year old Nhlanhla on Thursday . We can also film with Hendrik Manye's family ..Hendrik was shot last week ,after gunfire from a local Pakistani shop in Kagiso . We can film with Zanele Majola ,in Kagiso ,who's baby died in the stampede on a small Somali shop that is now being rebuilt . If the Somali's come back to their shop we will request to film with them this week . Phindile Shabangu witnessed the stampede and saw what happened with the baby and she will talk to us .Zanele is grief stricken she says ...We have put in a request for David Makhura ,Premier , and Solomon Mokgale ,and will call Adam Habib ..for some perspective on the aftermath and the grief .Akash in Lenasia will also talk to us about his fears of being killed if he goes back into Orlando to his shop ....

Press Release:


After the Violence
In 2008 widespread xenophobic violence rocked the country. Seven years later, it seems little has changed as foreigners flee for their lives from locals looting their businesses. With blood on the streets and allegations that even the police are turning a blind eye, Carte Blanche asks - what’s really at the root of the Soweto attacks?


Script:


SCRIPT XENOPHOBIA
On Thursday last week the community of Snake Park, near Dobsonville , Soweto gathered to mourn the death of 14 year old Simphiwe Mahori who was killed January 19 after being accused of robbing a shop run by an armed Somali .
Politicians have described the subsequent looting frenzy as criminal. For over nine days looting and attacks spread and police used rubber bullets and tear gas against the crowds. By 22 January sixty eight suspects had been arrested .Thousands of Bengalis , Pakistanis, Ethiopians and Somalis were displaced .
At this time President Zuma was in Davos, Switzerland at the World Economic Forum .

Adam Habib “What kind of society are we becoming ,I mean in any civilized society this would be a tragedy of national proportions , nobody would even utter or pat themselves on the back and say at least we contained it .That would be suicidal for you to do, so, what do we do ?we pat ourselves on the back and say at least we contained it . What the hell is going on in our society that we have become so immune , are we losing any sense of being civilized? “


In the sprawling township of Kagiso ,near Krugersdorp and west of Johannesburg , many Somalian and Ethiopian traders are persecuted , desperate but still resilient . They are trying to pick up the pieces .

Vox pop one Ethiopian We don’t have nothing to protect ourselves …we are suffering too much…

Bongani link “This Ethiopian owned shop was one of the targets of the looting ,now the official explanation from the authorities is that is simply opportunistic crime but interestingly I spoke to the owner of the shop next door, now she wont come on camera , but she is Malawian and her shop wasn’t touched and she says the explanation she got from the looters was she’s their kind of African . “
Up the street Ethiopian Eyasa Aman’s shop is still empty, shelves bare and he has no assets left.
Sound up Ethiopian We lost everything , for myself I don’t have anything ,I have two shops and I don’t have now even one Zimbuck ,I lost everything ,I lost everything .
He and also thousands of Somalians had to flee their businesses and homes in the middle of the night .The Somalians took all their possessions to Mayfair far from their shops .Many of them have become resigned to attacks on their businesses and are used to moving their stock away at a moments notice .


Councillor Peter Mokoena Now we are living in a democratic country ,we are living like maybe ,I should take you as my brother ,I should take someone from outside our country as my brother, as long as you are my brother .

We spoke to Professor Ingrid Palmary from the African Centre for Migration .She’s been tracking xenophobia for ten years .
Sound up Ingrid
Well I think we can expect to see on going violence this is not going to go away and I think if we made any mistake in 2008 it was imagining that this is over .I think this time we shouldn’t make the same mistake .

In Kagiso in 16 th street a week after the looting, one Somalian shop keeper is persistently back in business selling cut price goods.
LINK Bongani Theres no doubt theres a big element of opportunistic crime in the looting that occurred here but its also interesting that talking to the neighbours they all say most of the looters came from a different area but when they made the call to the police some of them had to squeeze out of a very tiny space as a result a baby died .

We obtained footage of the scene at the Somalian shop where the tragedy occurred .
Sound up Adam Habib “Imagine a cauldron of bubbling anger and there’s a flare up here and a flare up there and theres a flare up there and every time what we’re doing is we are rushing the police here and we are rushing the police there and we are looking at local solutions but there isn’t a comprehensive attempt to diffuse ,to bring down the heat so that the thing dosent simmer in the way that it is .

Bongani asks MEC “What did we learn from 2008 that would now apply ?

MEC says We have forums now of foreign nationals who have identified leaders of the communities and we worked with them during these particular attacks .I think because we are working with organized groups the impact was a little better .

Forums may have been started but since the xenophobic violence of 2008 sporadic unrest has not abated , and evidence has emerged proving that some members of the South African police ignored the looting.
In 2008 of course xenophobic violence came to the fore but in fact there has been ongoing attacks against foreigners ever since then,it didn’t stop in 2008 .And in fact more people have died since then .


Adam Habib
I think we saw the police move in on one level the police tried to contain it and there was quick action ,on another level it was atrocious ,you saw the front page newspaper and photographs of police looking around while people are looting and in one or two cases even police walking around with a whole series of things ,I mean that’s totally unacceptable.

National Spokesperson for the South African Police Service ,Solomon Makgale answered the criticisms.
Bongani question to General Makgale ‘Whats your response to the allegation that some officers were complicit in the looting or at least turned a blind eye ?

General Makgale “We have evidence of some police officers looting ,we have taken action against those police officers as we are speaking now there are three police officers that appeared in Galeshewe magistrates court for robbing a spaza shop ,two constables and a reservist.We have one police officer in Soweto who was also captured on video stealing from a spaza shop .We do not condone criminality by police officers ,not at all .

These looters had been arrested and were under restraint before getting taken away in a police vehicle .
General Makgale “ We obviously have learnt from the 2008 challenges but we also deal a lot of this unrest ,so we have gained a lot of experience ,in fact we are waiting on getting even more capacity to be able to address community unrest out of the blue ,just comes up .

Ingrid “It dosent come from nowhere there is often an undercurrent of hostility that predicts it.


Sometimes police frustration boils over …
Adam Habib “ I would have liked to have seen the national leadership descend on Soweto and say what the hell is going on ,this is unacceptable . Walk the talk on this matter . That’s not what happened .For me that is the real tragedy .

Criticism remains of the lack of leadership from government .
ZUMA STILL HERE
Bongani Why has the president not spoken out on this ?

MEC Sizakele Nkosi Malobane ,Gauteng Department of Community Safety
“He did ,he also instructed to us to make sure we protect the foreign nationals ,but also we protect South Africans .He also actually instructed us to make sure that no one dies .You know his first words to us as people who are dealing with this problem ,particularly the Premier who is the leadership ,was make sure that no one dies ,during this unrest ,and we did exactly that. But of course unfortunately about four people died under unfortunate circumstances .
Adam Habib You can go to Davos as much as you want ,you can take as many people as you want to Davos , and sell Team South Africa line as much as you want ,when those people see on their screens a flare up in Soweto where
Or Marikana they are saying what is the stability of my investment ?you can sell them as much as you want about how we got a handle on this thing etc, would you invest in Somalia ? would you invest in a place like the Ukraine now ,then ask yourself is it unreasonable for guys in Davos or who ever makes investment decisions to look around ….the presidency says we got this thing under control ,team South Africa is working and there youre having a flare up in Soweto and you have ESKOM doing the kind of things its doing ,you have the flare up in Marikana ,that is not a sustainable model for beginning to right the wrongs of this country .


Bongani stand up
The shooting and killing of fourteen year old Simphiwe Mahori is what sparked this latest round of shooting and killing and here at his memorial service the police are maintaining a visible presence and keeping things under control, which has been the hallmark of this latest spate of attacks ,unlike 2008 it hasn’t spread as far and wide .
But the community of Snake Park grieve the loss of a teenager and fear that more deaths may come .

VISUALS Sowetans singing at the memorial for teenager
